offence_severity: Minimum 6 years rigorous imprisonment / Maximum 10 years rigorous imprisonment
physical_harm: Victim died due to stab injury causing hemorrhage and shock
number_of_offences: Five accused charged; conviction upheld for four accused under different sections, one acquitted
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the medical evidence that Mitthulal died due to syncope on account of shock and hemorrhage caused by the stab injury inflicted by accused Gopal.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that the prosecution examined 13 witnesses and the defense examined two, and the Trial Court found them guilty based on the evidence.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 30.6.1992 and 1.7.1992; Trial judgment: 31.3.1995; High Court decision: 19.10.2005; Supreme Court decision: May 19, 2011
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: A S.K. Dubey, Subhash Kaushik, Malini Poduval, Praveena Gautam, C.D. Singh, Vikas Bansal, Vibha Datta Makhija, Vartika Sahay, Malini Poduval for the Appellant. Counsel for the State: Mr. S.K. Dubey
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction and sentence awarded; High Court: Accused Gopal convicted under s.304 (Part I) IPC, sentenced to 10 years; other accused convicted under s.324 IPC, let off on period already undergone; Supreme Court: Conviction of accused Gopal upheld, sentence reduced to period already undergone; appeal by State dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that accused Gopal deserves to be convicted under Section 302 IPC, even though he might have inflicted only a single injury on the chest of Mitthulal, as Mitthulal died instantaneously, showing the nature and force of the injury. The prosecution also contended that other accused persons could not have been convicted only under Section 324 IPC, as the injuries sustained by the complainant party were serious in nature, and the sentence of period already undergone with fine was too lenient.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the complainant party was the aggressor and that the accused acted in self-defence. It was also contended that the prosecution failed to explain the injuries sustained by Shankarlal and Gopal, and that the complainant party attacked the accused Shankarlal and Gopal while returning to Ratlam, causing injuries to them.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the ends of justice should be met, and that the conviction of accused Gopal under Section 304 Part-I IPC should be upheld, but his sentence should be reduced to the period already undergone by him, which was more than six years.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed to meet the ends of justice, reducing the sentence of accused Gopal to the period already undergone by him, which was more than six years.
